title: Equivariant resolution of one split marked nodal curve over a smooth pair
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S$ an integral finite-type $F$-scheme, and $D\subseteq S$ a closed subset [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $f:T\to S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Nodal means that the completed geometric local ring at a nonsmooth point is $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$. Assume $f$ is smooth over $S\setminus D$, and let $M$ be a finite disjoint union of sections in its relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let a finite group $J$ act on $F,T,S$ compatibly with $f$, preserving $D$ and $M$. Assume the marked nodal curve is split: fibre components, nodes and two branches descend to the residue field, and point stabilizers in $S$ act trivially on the fibre dual graph with marked legs. Let $t:S_0\to S$ be an equivariant projective birational surjection, where $S_0$ is integral and smooth over $F$ and the reduced inverse image of $D$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor $E$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. There is a $J$-equivariant projective birational surjection $r:T'\to T\times_SS_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with $T'$ integral and smooth over $F$. The composite $T'\to T$ is also projective birational and surjective. The map $r$ is an isomorphism outside the pullback of $|M|\cup f^{-1}D$, and the reduced inverse image of that closed set is a relative strict normal crossings divisor $E'$ on $T'/F$. Every local ring of $T'$ is regular, and the components of $E'$ through a point have local equations which are distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-regular-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. If $S_0$ is projective over $F$ in the finite-projective-space convention, $T'$ is projective over $F$ in that convention [def-kun-projective]. Birational means an isomorphism between dense opens and equality of function fields. Empty $D$ and $M$ are allowed. The case $t=\mathrm{id}$ includes resolution of a marked nodal curve directly over a smooth SNC pair.
